_comment: Hand-authored curation for the opening trainer. This is the ONLY file you edit
to add or change what the app teaches — everything else is generated.
Each line gives its moves in SAN. The build script replays them, validates every
move is legal, and attaches the official ECO code + name by longest-prefix match
against the lichess ECO dataset in eco-source/. You do not write the ECO code or
the official name yourself; that would drift.
'side' is the colour the LEARNER plays, so it decides which plies they answer.
'ideas' is index-aligned with the moves and may be shorter, sparse, or absent —
the UI renders fine without it. Write them for the learner's own moves; an idea
on an opponent move is never shown.

repertoires.title: The Italian Game
repertoires.blurb: The oldest opening in chess. Quick development, and the bishop points straight at Black's weakest square.

lines.label: Giuoco Piano
lines.labelOkWhy: the dataset calls this the Italian Classical Variation
lines.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bc4 Bc5 4. c3 Nf6 5. d4 exd4 6. cxd4 Bb4+ 7. Bd2
ideas: Claim the centre and open lines for the bishop and queen.
Develop with a threat — the knight already eyes e5.
The Italian bishop. It stares at f7, the square only the king defends.
Quiet but purposeful: c3 prepares to build the big centre with d4.
Now the centre breaks open while you are the better developed side.
Recapture toward the centre. You have pawns on d4 and e4 — the ideal pair.
Block the check and offer a trade. Your centre survives intact.

lines.label: Giuoco Pianissimo
lines.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bc4 Bc5 4. d3 Nf6 5. c3 d6 6. O-O
ideas: The 'very quiet game'. Support e4 and keep every piece defended.
Prepare d4 at leisure. There is no hurry in a closed position.
Castle first, decide on a plan second.

lines.label: Two Knights Defense
lines.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bc4 Nf6 4. Ng5 d5 5. exd5 Na5 6. Bb5+ c6 7. dxc6 bxc6
ideas: Crude but strong: two pieces now hit f7 and Black must react.
Take the pawn and keep the extra material for now.
Check, and hang on to the pawn a little longer.
Grab it. Black gets fast development for the pawn — play carefully.

lines.label: Evans Gambit
lines.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bc4 Bc5 4. b4 Bxb4 5. c3 Ba5 6. d4 exd4 7. O-O
ideas: A pawn for time. Deflect the bishop so you can build the centre with tempo.
Hit the bishop again and prepare d4 — every move comes with a threat.
Cash the gambit in: a huge centre while Black is still untangling.
Castle. Down a pawn, but far ahead in development and with open lines.

repertoires.title: The Ruy Lopez
repertoires.blurb: The Spanish Game. World champions have leaned on it for 150 years — slow pressure rather than a quick punch.

lines.label: Closed, Morphy Defense
lines.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bb5 a6 4. Ba4 Nf6 5. O-O Be7 6. Re1 b5 7. Bb3 d6 8. c3 O-O
ideas: Claim the centre.
Develop and attack e5.
Pressure the knight that defends e5 — the real point of the Ruy Lopez.
Keep the bishop on the a2-g8 diagonal rather than trading it off.
Castle. You can afford to ignore the e4 pawn for one move.
Defend e4 properly and put the rook on the file it belongs on.
Retreat again — this bishop is your best piece, don't let it go.
The Spanish move. Build a retreat square on c2 and prepare d4.

lines.label: Berlin Defense
lines.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bb5 Nf6 4. O-O Nxe4 5. d4 Nd6 6. Bxc6 dxc6 7. dxe5 Nf5 8. Qxd8+ Kxd8
ideas: Offer the e-pawn. Development matters more than the pawn here.
Strike in the centre while Black's knight is loose.
Trade to damage the pawn structure before Black consolidates.
Gain the pawn back and open the position.
The famous Berlin endgame. Black loses castling rights; you have the better structure.

lines.label: Exchange Variation
lines.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bb5 a6 4. Bxc6 dxc6 5. O-O
ideas: Trade at once. Black's doubled c-pawns are a permanent weakness in an endgame.
Castle. Your long-term plan is simply to reach an endgame.

lines.label: Open Variation
lines.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bb5 a6 4. Ba4 Nf6 5. O-O Nxe4 6. d4 b5 7. Bb3 d5 8. dxe5 Be6
ideas: Open the centre immediately to punish the wandering knight.
Retreat to safety on the strong diagonal.
Take, and accept a sharp middlegame with chances for both sides.

repertoires.title: The Scotch Game
repertoires.blurb: Break the centre open on move three. Far less theory than the Ruy Lopez, and it leads to open, tactical play.

lines.label: Classical Variation
lines.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. d4 exd4 4. Nxd4 Bc5 5. Be3 Qf6 6. c3 Nge7
ideas: Claim the centre.
Develop and attack e5.
Strike at once. No slow build-up here.
Recapture with the knight into the centre.
Defend the knight and blunt the bishop on the a7-g1 diagonal.
Shore up d4 and give the knight a home.

lines.label: Mieses Variation
lines.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. d4 exd4 4. Nxd4 Nf6 5. Nxc6 bxc6 6. e5 Qe7 7. Qe2 Nd5
ideas: Trade, saddling Black with doubled pawns.
Gain space and kick the knight before Black is organised.
Line the queen up on the e-file and hold the extra space.

lines.label: Scotch Gambit
lines.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. d4 exd4 4. Bc4 Nf6 5. e5 d5 6. Bb5 Ne4 7. Nxd4
ideas: Skip the recapture — develop, and aim at f7 instead.
Gain space with tempo before Black is organised.
Pin the knight and hold the tension.
Finally regain the pawn, with a free game and the better structure.

repertoires.title: Queen's Gambit Declined
repertoires.blurb: The classical way to play 1.d4. Not really a gambit — you almost always get the pawn back.

lines.label: Exchange Variation
lines.moves: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. cxd5 exd5 5. Bg5 Be7 6. e3 O-O
ideas: Take your share of the centre and open lines for the dark-squared bishop.
Challenge d5 from the side. This is the gambit — it is only a loan.
Develop and add a third attacker to d5.
Release the tension on your terms and fix Black's structure.
Pin the knight, making d5 harder to hold.
Modest, but it frees the light-squared bishop and secures d4.

lines.label: Tartakower Defense
lines.moves: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. Bg5 Be7 5. e3 O-O 6. Nf3 h6 7. Bh4 b6
ideas: Pin the f6 knight before Black can castle out of it.
Solid and flexible.
Complete the kingside development.
Keep the pin rather than conceding the bishop pair.

lines.label: Tarrasch Defense
lines.moves: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 c5 4. cxd5 exd5 5. Nf3 Nc6 6. g3
ideas: Take, giving Black an isolated d-pawn to look after.
Develop and put more pressure on d4 and d5.
The critical plan: fianchetto and blockade the isolated pawn on d5.

repertoires.title: The London System
repertoires.blurb: The same setup against almost anything Black plays. The lowest-theory way to start a serious 1.d4 repertoire.

lines.label: Main Line
lines.moves: 1. d4 d5 2. Bf4 Nf6 3. e3 e6 4. Nf3 c5 5. c3 Nc6 6. Nbd2 Bd6 7. Bg3
ideas: Take the centre.
The London move. Get the bishop outside the pawn chain before playing e3.
Now the pawn can come to e3 without burying the bishop.
Develop naturally. The setup is the same whatever Black does.
Support d4 so the centre never collapses.
The knight belongs here, keeping the c-pawn's path clear.
Sidestep the trade and keep the bishop on its best diagonal.

lines.label: vs King's Indian setup
lines.labelOkWhy: label describes what Black set up, not the opening name
lines.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. Bf4 g6 3. e3 Bg7 4. Nf3 O-O 5. Be2 d6 6. h3
ideas: The bishop comes out first, as always.
Complete the pawn triangle — same setup, whatever Black builds.
Develop naturally.
Modest square, but it keeps everything defended.
Give the bishop an escape square before Black plays ...Nh5 to trade it.

lines.label: vs early ...c5
lines.moves: 1. d4 d5 2. Bf4 c5 3. e3 Nc6 4. c3 Nf6 5. Nd2
ideas: Solidify.
Hold the centre together — c3 and e3 make d4 very hard to shift.
Develop flexibly and keep the option of Ngf3.

repertoires.title: Sicilian: Najdorf
repertoires.blurb: The sharpest answer to 1.e4, and Fischer's and Kasparov's weapon of choice. You play for a win, not a draw.

lines.label: English Attack (6. Be3)
lines.moves: 1. e4 c5 2. Nf3 d6 3. d4 cxd4 4. Nxd4 Nf6 5. Nc3 a6 6. Be3 e5 7. Nb3 Be6
ideas: Fight for the centre without symmetry — this is why the Sicilian wins games.
Control e5 and prepare to develop.
Take. You trade a wing pawn for a centre pawn, a small structural win.
Develop with a hit on e4.
The Najdorf move. Tiny, but it takes b5 away from White's pieces for good.
Grab the centre now that White's knight has nowhere good to go.
Cover d5, the one square Black's structure genuinely concedes.

lines.label: Main Line (6. Bg5)
lines.moves: 1. e4 c5 2. Nf3 d6 3. d4 cxd4 4. Nxd4 Nf6 5. Nc3 a6 6. Bg5 e6 7. f4 Be7
ideas: Solid. Break the pin's sting before grabbing space.
Unpin, and prepare to castle out of the coming attack.

lines.label: Classical (6. Be2)
lines.labelOkWhy: Opocensky is the dataset name for the 6.Be2 Najdorf
lines.moves: 1. e4 c5 2. Nf3 d6 3. d4 cxd4 4. Nxd4 Nf6 5. Nc3 a6 6. Be2 e5 7. Nb3 Be7
ideas: Against a quiet bishop move, take the centre at once.
Develop and castle quickly — White has no fast attack here.

repertoires.title: Sicilian: Accelerated Dragon
repertoires.blurb: A Sicilian with far less theory than the Najdorf. The bishop on g7 does the work.

lines.label: Main Line
lines.moves: 1. e4 c5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. d4 cxd4 4. Nxd4 g6 5. Nc3 Bg7 6. Be3 Nf6 7. Bc4 O-O
ideas: The Sicilian. Unbalance the position from move one.
Develop and fight for d4.
Take — a wing pawn for a centre pawn.
Prepare the fianchetto. Saving a tempo over the normal Dragon is the whole point.
The bishop's diagonal is the soul of this opening.
Develop, and keep an eye on the d5 square.
Castle into safety before White organises an attack.

lines.label: Maroczy Bind
lines.moves: 1. e4 c5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. d4 cxd4 4. Nxd4 g6 5. c4 Nf6 6. Nc3 d6 7. Be2 Nxd4 8. Qxd4 Bg7
ideas: Develop with a hit on e4 before White finishes the bind.
Solid. Take d5 and e5 away from White's pieces.
Trade off a strong knight to relieve the cramp.
Finally the bishop comes to life on the long diagonal.

repertoires.title: The French Defense
repertoires.blurb: Solid and strategic. You concede space early and spend the game undermining White's centre.

lines.label: Winawer Variation
lines.moves: 1. e4 e6 2. d4 d5 3. Nc3 Bb4 4. e5 c5 5. a3 Bxc3+ 6. bxc3 Ne7
ideas: Prepare to challenge e4 with ...d5 next move.
Strike at the centre immediately.
Pin the knight that defends e4 — the sharpest reply.
Attack the base of the pawn chain. Always hit the bottom, not the top.
Take. White's doubled c-pawns are a long-term target.
Route the knight to f5 where it hits the weak d4 pawn.

lines.label: Classical Variation
lines.moves: 1. e4 e6 2. d4 d5 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. Bg5 Be7 5. e5 Nfd7 6. Bxe7 Qxe7
ideas: Develop and add pressure to e4.
Break the pin calmly rather than weakening the kingside.
Retreat and keep the option of undermining with ...c5 and ...f6.
Recapture. The bishop trade has eased your cramped position.

lines.label: Tarrasch Variation
lines.moves: 1. e4 e6 2. d4 d5 3. Nd2 Nf6 4. e5 Nfd7 5. Bd3 c5 6. c3 Nc6
ideas: Develop, provoking White to commit the centre.
Retreat and regroup — the knight is heading for c5 or f8.
Strike the base of the chain.
Pile another attacker onto d4.

lines.label: Advance Variation
ideas: Hit the base of the chain at once — d4 is the target, not e5.
Add a second attacker to d4.
The standard plan: the queen hits d4 again and eyes the weak b2 pawn.

repertoires.title: The Caro-Kann
repertoires.blurb: As solid as the French, but the light-squared bishop gets out first. A favourite of players who hate bad positions.

lines.label: Classical Variation
lines.moves: 1. e4 c6 2. d4 d5 3. Nc3 dxe4 4. Nxe4 Bf5 5. Ng3 Bg6 6. h4 h6
ideas: Prepare ...d5 — but with the c-pawn, so the bishop stays free.
Challenge the centre on equal terms.
Release the tension and remove White's best pawn.
The whole point of the Caro-Kann: this bishop gets out before ...e6 locks it in.
Retreat and keep the good bishop.

lines.label: Advance Variation
ideas: Develop the bishop outside the chain before playing ...e6.
Now ...e6 costs nothing — the bishop is already out.
Strike the base of the pawn chain.

lines.label: Exchange Variation
lines.moves: 1. e4 c6 2. d4 d5 3. exd5 cxd5 4. Bd3 Nc6 5. c3 Nf6
ideas: Recapture toward the centre and open the c-file.
Develop and pressure d4.
Develop and fight for control of e4.

lines.label: Panov Attack
lines.moves: 1. e4 c6 2. d4 d5 3. exd5 cxd5 4. c4 Nf6 5. Nc3 e6
ideas: Develop and defend d5 — White is playing for an isolated pawn structure.
Solid. Hold d5 and accept a rich middlegame.
